response.sql: WITH per_name AS (SELECT r.name, AVG(ds.points) AS avg_points, COUNT(*) AS field_size FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(field_size) AS avg_field FROM per_name) SELECT AVG(p.avg_points) AS avg_of_avg_points, AVG(p.field_size) AS avg_field_size, AVG(p.field_size - o.avg_field) AS avg_excess_field_size FROM per_name p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.field_size > o.avg_field

assumptions.assumption: Field size for a race name is the number of driverStandings rows joined to races with that name (across all years), via an inner join so standings without a matching race are dropped.
The overall average field size is the unweighted mean of field sizes across race names, and the excess is each qualifying race name's field size minus that mean, averaged.
AVG ignores NULL points, as the request specifies.

alternatives.interpretation: Field size is the number of distinct drivers appearing in the standings for that race name, rather than the number of standings rows.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_name AS (SELECT r.name, AVG(ds.points) AS avg_points, COUNT(DISTINCT ds.driverId) AS field_size FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(field_size) AS avg_field FROM per_name) SELECT AVG(p.avg_points) AS avg_of_avg_points, AVG(p.field_size) AS avg_field_size, AVG(p.field_size - o.avg_field) AS avg_excess_field_size FROM per_name p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.field_size > o.avg_field
